text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin assessing your sudden-onset vertigo, can you describe whether the sensation feels like the room is spinning around you or if you feel like you are swaying or falling? Also, did this episode start suddenly while you were resting or did it begin when you moved your head in a specific direction?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since the episode was brief and you are currently back to baseline, do you currently experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in either ear? Additionally, does moving your head to the right or left side, or rolling over in bed, trigger the spinning sensation again?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the symptoms started while going to bed, but you haven't answered my previous questions yet. Please tell me if you have any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear fullness, and whether rolling over or moving your head triggers the spinning sensation again.

speaker: Doctor

The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver on the left side, combined with the brief duration of symptoms and lack of auditory findings, strongly indicates Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) of the left posterior canal. I am confident in this clinical diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
